data.name: Jyotindri
data.long_meaning: Jyotindri is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'jyoti' (light) and 'indri' (goddess or ruler). In Hindu mythology, Jyotindri is the goddess of light and knowledge, believed to bestow wisdom and illumination upon her devotees. She is often depicted holding a lamp or a torch in her hands, symbolizing the dispeller of darkness and ignorance.

historical_references.reference: Jyotindri was a renowned Hindu scholar during the Gupta Empire (4th to 6th century CE). He was a disciple of the famous philosopher and polymath, Vallabhacharya, who was known for his contributions to mathematics, astronomy, and religion. Jyotindri is best remembered for his works on Jyotisha (Indian astronomy) and Mimamsa philosophy.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Jyotindri can be found in the Puranic literature, specifically in the Mahabharata, where he is mentioned as one of the great sages and seers of ancient India. He is believed to have lived during the Treta Yuga (second of the four yugas in Hindu cosmology), which is traditionally dated to around 3102–2900 BCE. Jyotindri is revered in Hinduism for his deep wisdom and spiritual insights.
